facts.statement: The genus Palaeocarcharodon was named by Casier in 1960.
facts.quote: authority: Casier, 1960

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Carcharodon orientalis.
facts.quote: type_species: Carcharodon orientalis

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon landanensis has been proposed as a synonym of Carcharodon orientalis.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Carcharodon orientalis? Sinzow, 1899 Palaeocarcharodon landanensis? (Casier, 1960) Carcharodon landanensis? Leriche, 1942

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon lived between 61.7 and 55.8 million years ago during the Middle Paleocene and Early Eocene.
facts.quote: lived about 61.7 to 55.8 Ma during the Middle Paleocene and Early Eocene

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon is also known as the pygmy white shark.
facts.quote: Palaeocarcharodon, also known as the pygmy white shark

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon is classified within the family Cretoxyrhinidae.
facts.quote: genus of shark within the family Cretoxyrhinidae

facts.statement: The genus Palaeocarcharodon currently contains only one valid species, P. orientalis.
facts.quote: It currently contains a sole species P. orientalis

facts.statement: Sinzow originally named the species Carcharodon orientalis in 1899.
facts.quote: Sinzow (1899) named the shark as a new species of the genus Carcharodon, as C. orientalis

facts.statement: The classification of Palaeocarcharodon remains a subject of debate among researchers.
facts.quote: As is the case with most sharks, the classification of Palaeocarcharodon is still debated

facts.statement: In 2013, some researchers suggested that P. landanensis is a senior synonym of P. orientalis, though this is still debated.
facts.quote: In 2013, it was suggested that P. landanensis could be a senior synonym of P. orientalis, among other older articles

facts.statement: While some theories placed Palaeocarcharodon in the family Otodontidae, recent papers generally classify it in Cretoxyrhinidae.
facts.quote: In the same year, it was theorized that Palaeocarcharodon was a member of Otodontidae, however, currently many recent papers place it in the family Cretoxyrhinidae

facts.statement: Some teeth found in Volgograd, Russia, lack serrations and are classified as Palaeocarcharodon cf. orientalis.
facts.quote: Some teeth found in Russia, in Volgograd, show Palaeocarcharodon without serrations

facts.statement: The exact size of Palaeocarcharodon is uncertain.
facts.quote: Like most prehistoric sharks, Palaeocarcharodon has an uncertain size

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon is estimated to have been comparable in size to mako sharks or modern great white sharks.
facts.quote: it is estimated that it was comparable in size to mako sharks or the modern great white shark

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon teeth were triangular, compressed, and featured irregular serrations with serrate lateral cusplets.
facts.quote: Teeth of Palaeocarcharodon are triangular, labio-lingually compressed, with quite irregular serrations and serrate lateral cusplets

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon teeth could reach a length of about 3 to 6 centimeters.
facts.quote: They can reach a size of about 3 - 6 cm

facts.statement: Fossil evidence for Palaeocarcharodon consists of a few possible vertebrae and several teeth.
facts.quote: currently being known by a few possible vertebrae and several teeth

facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeocarcharodon have been found in the Americas, Asia, Russia, North Africa, and Europe.
facts.quote: Fossils of Palaeocarcharodon have been found in the Americas, Asia, Russia, North Africa, and Europe

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Palaeocarcharodon as Otodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Otodontidae

facts.statement: Palaeocarcharodon belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
facts.quote: Class: Chondrichthyes

facts.statement: The time range for Palaeocarcharodon is recorded as the Danian to Priabonian stages, from 66 to 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Priabonian (66 to 33.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Palaeocarcharodon had a body made primarily of cartilage rather than bone.
rejected.quote: Like most sharks, Palaeocarcharodon had a body made primarily of cartilage, not bone
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Palaeocarcharodon had a body made primarily of cartilage'
